extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents/applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, citing, and framing Office actions during patent examination, including citation of references, completeness and clarity of actions, treatment of applicant arguments, and handling allowable subject matter and claim status. Directed primarily at patent examiners (with relevance to applicants/agents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of electronic and nontraditional references
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples and formats for citing documents retrieved from online sources, Internet URLs, FTP, electronic serials, bulletin boards, e-mail, datasheets, and CD-ROM products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full citation information including author/title, platform (e.g., [online]), date retrieved, source (e.g., EPO PAJ Database, CAS on CD), and URL where available. Use specific examples (book/report, chapter, electronic serial, bulletin boards, contributions, electronic mail, product manuals/datasheets, industrial design database entries) to illustrate acceptable citation forms. Include ISSN or other identifiers when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates of declassified printed matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When using declassified material as a reference, consider both the printing date (when prepared for limited distribution) and the publication date (date of public release).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of release following declassification is the effective date of publication for anticipation. If release date not shown, determine it by reference to Office of Technical Services. Declassified material may be prima facie evidence of prior knowledge as of its printing date even if classified then; such printing dates may be antedated by affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect citation correction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure when a citation of a reference is found to be in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant notifies Office, send correction letter with correct copy of reference. If examiner discovers error, notify applicant and restart reply period. Examiner must correct the error in ink on the paper, initial the correction, and note the paper number of the action in which citation is corrected. Use form paragraphs 7.81–7.83 (e.g., 7.81 Correction Letter; 7.82 Correction of Reference Citation; 7.82.01 Copy of Reference(s) Furnished; 7.83 Copy of Office Action Supplied) and supply PTO-892 where applicable. For foreign patent citation errors, contact the General Reference Branch/technical library for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of decisions, orders, memorandums, and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cite court decisions, Board decisions, and Office orders or memoranda in official actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the USPQ citation and, when convenient, the U.S., CCPA, or Federal Reporter citation. Avoid citing manuscript decisions not publicly available. A federal district court decision reversed on appeal cannot be cited as authority. If citing an unpublished but publicly available manuscript decision, identify tribunal and complete data (e.g., paper number, patent number, page count). When citing a Director's order/notice/memo not yet in the MPEP, give title and date and other locating data (e.g., Official Gazette or JPTO Society Journal issue). Cite decisions found only in patent files only when no published decision exists on the point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action (37 CFR 1.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's action should be complete as to all matters, except in appropriate limited circumstances (misjoinder, fundamental defects, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable. Limit actions only where appropriate; otherwise address all substantive matters in the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete action on formal matters in first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal informalities should be listed and included with the examiner's first action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forms (e.g., PTO-948) listing informalities noted and mail them with the examiner's first action; include any additional formal requirements the examiner wants raised. For IFW (Image File Wrapper) processing, follow IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: When formal requirements are made where subject matter is allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: If an action indicates allowable subject matter but also makes formal requirements, the action must advise the applicant how to reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call attention to 37 CFR 1.111(b) and state that a complete reply must either comply with all formal requirements or specifically traverse each requirement not complied with. Use ¶ 7.43.03 (Allowable Subject Matter, Formal Requirements Outstanding) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner tone and affirmative identification of allowable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid personal opinions about lack of patentable merit; identify claims judged allowable and suggest ways to amend rejected claims to make them allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not express that an application 'appears to be' devoid of patentable subject matter. As part of first merit action, identify any claims judged allowable, and suggest amendments to rejected claims. If patentable subject matter is apparent but not properly claimed (especially for pro se applicants), consider drafting claims or suggesting allowance and mentioning possible desirability of an interview to accelerate agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and specificity to be used in rejecting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Required phrasing and clarity when rejecting claims on substantive grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the word 'rejected' for substantive refusals and fully and clearly state the ground of rejection. The opening sentence of each ground should expressly reference the statutory basis (e.g., 35 U.S.C. section). If a claim is rejected as broader than the enabling disclosure, explain why; if rejected as indefinite, point out where indefiniteness resides; if incomplete, specify missing elements. Avoid personal remarks. Avoid omnibus rejections like 'on the references and for the reasons of record' and avoid grouping claims together in a common rejection unless equally applicable to all claims in the group. See MPEP § 706.02(i),(j),(m) for language to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note all outstanding requirements in subsequent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking up an amended application, every outstanding requirement should be noted to prevent implied waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat or refer to every point in the prior action still applicable, including requirements under 37 CFR 1.105 and MPEP § 704.10. Determine whether requirements have been satisfied by a negative reply under 37 CFR 1.105(a)(3). As soon as allowable subject matter is found, require correction of all informalities then present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer all material traversed and asserted advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide clear explanations of actions taken and must address applicant traversals and asserted advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make proper reference to traversed requirements and, if the applicant traverses a rejection, answer the substance of the argument. If applicant's arguments are persuasive and the rejection is withdrawn, provide reasons in the next communication referring to specific pages/lines of applicant's remarks (do not merely say 'all remarks'). If withdrawal results in allowance, include reasons for allowance. If withdrawing and asserting a new ground, explain the new ground and consider finality under MPEP § 706.07(a). If the asserted advantages are not sufficient, state reasons in the record so applicant and the Board are informed. See MPEP §§ 716 et seq. for handling affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132. Use form paragraphs 7.37–7.38.02 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use when applicant's arguments are not persuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ¶ 7.37 and subparagraphs to state when applicant's arguments have been considered but are not persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 7.37 template: indicate arguments considered but not persuasive and provide explanation. Use the appropriate subparagraph (e.g., 7.37.01–7.37.13) to address specific common argument types and include an explanation of non-persuasiveness in bracketed insertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When applicant's arguments are persuasive and prior rejection/objection withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: If arguments are persuasive, withdraw the prior rejection/objection and state the basis for withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 7.38.01 to notify that applicant's arguments were persuasive, identify page(s)/line(s) of applicant's remarks forming basis for withdrawal, and indicate what rejection/objection was withdrawn and to which claims/figures/specification parts it pertains.

rubrics_metrics.name: When applicant's arguments are persuasive but new ground(s) of rejection are made
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant's arguments show problems with prior rejection but examiner finds different grounds, withdraw prior rejection and state new ground(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 7.38.02: identify applicant's remarks relied upon, state the prior statutory basis withdrawn, and insert the new ground(s) (e.g., different interpretation of reference, newly found prior art) with explanation. Provide claim numbers and statutory bases as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Age of references
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's contention that references are 'old' is generally not persuasive without showing that the art tried and failed to solve the same problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference In re Wright. Use ¶ 7.37.01 following ¶ 7.37 and explain why age alone does not negate relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Bodily incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness is not tested by whether features of a secondary reference can be bodily incorporated into a primary reference or whether the claimed invention is expressly suggested in any single reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that the test is what the combined teachings would have suggested to one of ordinary skill in the art (In re Keller). Use ¶ 7.37.02 and restate applicant's argument briefly as bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Hindsight reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconstruction based on hindsight is acceptable so long as it uses knowledge within the ordinary skill at the time and does not include applicant's disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re McLaughlin. Use ¶ 7.37.03 and explain that some reconstructive reasoning is inherent in obviousness determinations but must be limited to prior art knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: No suggestion to combine
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness by combination requires some teaching, suggestion, or motivation to combine references, either in the references themselves or in the general knowledge of one of ordinary skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify where the motivation for the combination is found (in references or knowledge generally available). Cite In re Fine and In re Jones. Use ¶ 7.37.04 and explain specifics in bracketed insert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Nonanalogous art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art reference must be either in the field of the applicant's endeavor or reasonably pertinent to the problem to be relied upon as a basis for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the reference is analogous art and identify the reference name. Cite In re Oetiker. Use ¶ 7.37.05 with bracketed explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Number of references
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on many references alone does not weigh against obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Gorman. Use ¶ 7.37.06 to reject argument that combining an 'excessive' number of references makes the combination improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Applicant obtains result not contemplated by prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of another advantage flowing naturally from following prior art does not establish patentability when differences would otherwise be obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Ex parte Obiaya. Use ¶ 7.37.07 and restate applicant's contention briefly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Arguing limitations which are not claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations from the specification are not read into the claims; arguments relying on features not recited in the rejected claim are unpersuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Van Geuns. Use ¶ 7.37.08 and note that claimed language controls; briefly recite the features applicant relies on as bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: A recitation of intended use must result in a structural difference to be accorded patentable weight; if prior art structure is capable of the intended use it meets the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 7.37.09 and briefly restate applicant's intended-use argument; explain why intended use alone does not distinguish structurally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Limitations in a preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: A preamble generally is not accorded patentable weight where it merely recites purpose or intended use and the body of the claim stands alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Hirao and Kropa v. Robie. Use ¶ 7.37.10 and restate the preamble recitation briefly; explain when preamble language is not given weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: General allegation of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: General allegations that the claims define a patentable invention without specific pointing out of distinctions fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 7.37.11 and explain that applicant must specifically point out how claim language distinguishes over cited art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Novelty not clearly pointed out
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that do not clearly point out the patentable novelty in view of the references fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 7.37.12 and explain that applicant must show how amendments avoid references/objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive argument: Attacking references individually when combination is relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot show nonobviousness by attacking references individually where rejections are based on combinations of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Keller and In re Merck. Use ¶ 7.37.13 and explain that combined teachings must be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of piecemeal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should avoid piecemeal examination; ordinarily reject each claim on all valid grounds while avoiding undue multiplication of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply major technical rejections (lack of disclosure, enablement, serious indefiniteness, res judicata) with full development of reasons rather than stereotyped conclusions. Do not make secondary minor rejections where prior art discloses the 'heart' of the invention. Situations allowing limited action include: application too informal, undue multiplicity of claims without election, misjoinder of inventions, or disclosure directed to perpetual motion. Where res judicata or other major grounds apply, accompany with other available grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify of inaccuracies in amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If inaccuracies are found in amendments, notify as required (see MPEP § 714 II.G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP § 714 subsection II.G for procedures; ensure applicants are informed of any inaccuracies found in amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each claim must be mentioned in each Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Every pending claim should be mentioned by number and its treatment or status given in each Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a summary of status of all claims presented for examination; use Form PTO-326 'Office Action Summary'. Maintain Index of Claims per MPEP § 719.04. Claims retained under specific CFR provisions should be treated per MPEP § 821–821.04(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: State when claims are allowable and offer constructive assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: When patentable subject matter is found or claims would be allowable if corrected, the examiner should state this and offer constructive suggestions (including drafting claims for pro se applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pro se applicants, examiner may draft claim(s) and indicate they would be allowed if incorporated (¶ 7.43.04). If claims are allowable except as to form, provide definite suggestions for correction and consider recommending an interview. Where claims are otherwise allowable but dependent on cancelled/rejected claims, state they would be allowable if rewritten in independent form. Do not delay allowance of clearly allowable claims once prior art fully developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim allowable if rewritten to overcome 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dependent claim is rejected solely under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, it may be allowable if rewritten to include all limitations of the base claim and intervening claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 7.43.02 to indicate that claim [1] would be allowable if rewritten to overcome the 112 rejection; use only when dependent claim would be allowable after amendment as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion of allowable drafted claim(s) for pro se applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may draft and present suggested claim language to pro se applicants when such claims distinguish patentably over the art of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 7.43.04 to present suggested claim(s), insert complete text of suggested claim(s), and require supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 if appropriate. Use form paragraph 7.97 to indicate allowance of claims when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating allowance of claim(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal indication that a claim is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶ 7.97: 'Claim [1] allowed.' Form paragraphs 7.43, 7.43.01, and 7.43.02 may be used to indicate allowable subject matter prior to formal allowance.
